title: Europe and Central Asia Agree on a Roadmap for AI in Health
title_zh: 欧洲与中亚就卫生领域人工智能路线图达成一致
source_name: WHO/Europe — Governments across Europe and Central Asia unanimously adopt new vision for AI in health care
summary_zh: 世界卫生组织欧洲区域 53 个成员国于 2026 年 10 月 29 日一致通过该地区首份《人工智能卫生行动路线图》（2026–2033）。计划覆盖治理、伦理监管、数据基础设施和人员培训四大优先领域，强调人工智能可协助早诊、预警与减负，但必须安全、公平并保护隐私；护理的核心仍是人际联结，AI 应是助手而非替代。本文适合积累健康、科技与政策类雅思词汇。
paragraphs: On 29 October 2026, the 53 member states of the World Health Organization's European Region took a rare step together. At a meeting of health ministers in Copenhagen, they unanimously adopted the region's first "Roadmap for action on artificial intelligence in health". The plan runs from 2026 to 2033 and aims to bring AI into health systems across Europe and Central Asia in a safe and fair way.

AI is already changing daily medical work. It can help doctors detect diseases earlier, warn staff when a patient's condition gets worse, and cut the time spent on paperwork. Patients may also get basic answers about their symptoms at any hour of the day. Officials say these tools can support health workers and move countries closer to universal health coverage — care that everyone can use without facing financial hardship.

Yet the opportunities come with clear risks. How can governments make sure AI is safe, effective and fair? How can they protect people's private health data and earn public trust? No country can answer these questions alone. That is why the roadmap sets out a shared regional approach rather than leaving each nation to invent its own rules.

The document focuses on four linked priorities. First, governance and leadership: countries should place AI inside national health strategies and decide who is responsible for it. Second, ethical, legal and regulatory frameworks that encourage innovation while keeping people safe. Third, strong data and digital systems, including good data quality, secure access and cybersecurity. Fourth, training for the workforce so staff can use AI tools well and judge their results.

The roadmap builds on a 2025 assessment of AI readiness for health. Fifty of the region's 53 countries took part. It also aligns with wider European rules, such as the EU Artificial Intelligence Act and rules that protect personal data. Leaders stressed that the future of care still depends on human connection; AI should be an ally for patients and professionals, not a replacement for them.

For English learners preparing for IELTS, this story is useful practice. It combines health, technology and public policy — three common exam themes. Notice how the article moves from a concrete decision to opportunities, then to risks and finally to a structured plan. That pattern of problem–response–evaluation often appears in Reading and Writing Task 2.
paragraphs_zh: 2026年10月29日，世界卫生组织欧洲区域的53个成员国迈出了少见的共同一步。在哥本哈根举行的卫生部长会议上，他们一致通过了该地区首份《人工智能卫生行动路线图》。该计划覆盖2026年至2033年，目标是以安全、公平的方式，把人工智能引入欧洲和中亚各国的卫生系统。
人工智能已经在改变日常医疗工作。它可以帮助医生更早发现疾病，在患者病情恶化时向医护人员发出警报，并减少文书工作占用的时间。患者也可能在一天中的任何时段获得关于自身症状的基本解答。官员们表示，这些工具可以支持医护人员，并推动各国更接近全民健康覆盖——即人人都能获得医疗服务，而不至于陷入经济困境。
然而，机遇伴随着明确的风险。政府如何确保人工智能既安全、有效又公平？如何保护人们的私人健康数据并赢得公众信任？没有任何一个国家能单独回答这些问题。正因为如此，这份路线图提出的是一套共享的区域方案，而不是让每个国家各自制定规则。
文件聚焦四个相互关联的优先事项。第一，治理与领导力：各国应将人工智能纳入国家卫生战略，并明确责任归属。第二，伦理、法律与监管框架，既鼓励创新，又保障人身安全。第三，强大的数据与数字系统，包括良好的数据质量、安全访问和网络安全。第四，对劳动力进行培训，使工作人员能够用好人工智能工具并判断其结果。
该路线图建立在2025年一份关于卫生领域人工智能就绪程度评估的基础之上。该地区53个国家中有50个参与了评估。它还与更广泛的欧洲规则保持一致，例如欧盟《人工智能法案》以及保护个人数据的规定。领导人强调，未来的医疗护理仍取决于人与人之间的联结；人工智能应成为患者和专业人员的助手，而不是替代者。
对准备雅思的英语学习者来说，这篇报道很适合练习。它把健康、科技与公共政策三个常见考试话题结合在一起。注意文章如何从一项具体决定讲到机遇，再讲到风险，最后落到有条理的计划。这种「问题—应对—评价」的展开方式，在阅读和写作任务二中经常出现。
